docs.presetsBounds.component: The figures a designer actually reaches for, one page per helper: `rect`, `circle`, `ellipse`,
`polygon`, `star`, and the bendable `line`. Every one is an ORDINARY FUNCTION the kit exports,
returning the same `Shape` every other preset does — a start point and a list of segments, and
nothing that sorts one figure from another.
import { node, Bounded, rect, star } from "game-kit"
const card = node("card", Bounded({ bounds: rect(1, 1.4) }))
const badge = node("badge", Bounded({ bounds: star(5, 1, 0.42) }))
These used to share one page with `Atoms/Bounded`, behind a `preset` dropdown that could turn
any of the eight into any other. Which meant a page named `Circle` could show a `star` with one
click — a story that can become a different story is not honest about what it draws. So each
helper is on its own page now, with only its own numbers on the panel: `Rect` offers `w`, `h`
and `radius`; `Circle` offers `r`; nothing more, nothing borrowed from a neighbour.
The `preset` switcher itself still exists, unchanged, and is still exactly right for one page:
`Atoms/Surfaced → Plate`, whose whole lesson is "any shape the box can be". That is a different
claim from this shelf's "here is what each helper gives you", and the two are not the same page
What is NOT here: `Atoms/Bounded` keeps the pages about the FIELD rather than a named helper —
a raw value, a hand-typed path, a pasted SVG. This shelf is the ready-made half.
docs.presetsBounds.rect: `w` and `h` are the whole of it. Units, not pixels: the host decides what a unit is worth on
screen, so this card is the same card on a phone and on a desk monitor.
Bring `radius` up off zero and the very same call becomes `roundedRect(w, h, radius)` — one
preset, rounded by a number, rather than two sorts of box.
docs.presetsBounds.circle: One number, `r`. A circle has nothing else to say.
Inside it is four cubics and nothing more. It becomes a polygon only at the renderer:
`outlineOf` flattens the curves to straight runs against a tolerance measured in units, and for
`r: 0.8` that comes out at 64 points — below the model, which only ever holds a circle.
docs.presetsBounds.ellipse: `ellipse(1.2, 0.8)` — four cubics, and that is exactly what one is.
A circle is this with equal radii. Not a scaled circle, not a sort of its own: `circle(r)` is
one line that calls `ellipse(r, r)`. Saying it the other way round is what would put a tag in
the model for a shape one argument away from its neighbour.
docs.presetsBounds.polygon: `polygon(5, 0.9)` — N corners on a circle, the first one at the top.
The same helper draws a triangle, an octagon and a sixteen-sided coin. Nothing about it is a
special case: it returns a path of straight runs, exactly like the one you would paste.
docs.presetsBounds.star: `star(5, 1, 0.42)` — five points on the outer circle, the notches between them on the inner.
A polygon whose corners alternate between two radii, which is why it needs no new sort. The kit
does not know the word "star"; one helper does, and it is the only place that has to.
Bring the inner radius up towards the outer and it becomes a cog; take it down and the points
docs.presetsBounds.line: A run between two places — and the bend belongs to the BOX. `from` and `to` are the ends;
